Vuong test for non-nested or overlapping choice models

Source: R/compare.R
vuong.Rd

Vuong's (1989) test comparing two fits to the same cases; positive values favour the first model. It is the comparison the inflation literature uses between an inflated model and its uninflated counterpart (Bagozzi and Marchetti 2017; Greene 1994), where the restriction \(\phi = 1\) sits at the boundary so that the likelihood-ratio statistic is not chi-square. Its standard normal reference does not hold there: when the uninflated model is true the two models are nested at the boundary, the per-case differences degenerate, and the statistic is not N(0, 1) (Wilson 2015, on the same use for zero-inflated counts; a size study under the MNL null is part of the package's verification, verification/vuong_size_mc.R in the development repository). The calibrated alternative is the parametric bootstrap of the likelihood-ratio and Vuong statistics under the restricted model, boot_lr_test(). Between strictly non-nested models the normal reference holds; for overlapping ones (sharing some covariates) Vuong's procedure first tests whether the per-case differences have zero variance (the models are then equivalent on these data), which this function reports only as an error when the differences are identical. With frequency weights the statistic equals the one computed on duplicated cases. Reported with the raw numerator and with the AIC and BIC corrections for the difference in parameter counts. When the two fits are practically the same model on the data (one at the other's boundary, such as an inflated fit with \(\phi\) at 1), the per-case differences are round-off, every statistic divides by their spread, and the corrected ones run to minus millions: when that spread totals less than 0.01 (\(\sqrt{n}\,\hat\omega < 0.01\)) the statistics are NA and a note says the models cannot be told apart. When either model is a remnl() fit, whose likelihood is per unit, the contributions of both are summed by unit and the statistic (and the \(n\) of its BIC correction) is over units, while fit_stats() counts cases.

Usage

vuong(m1, m2)

Arguments

m1, m2

Two "choicemodel" fits to the same cases.

Value

A data frame of class "vuong" with one row per correction: statistic, p_m1_better (one-sided, m1 preferred), p_m2_better, and p_two_sided.

Details

The statistics assume independent cases: a fit's cluster does not enter them.

References

Bagozzi, B.E. and Marchetti, K. (2017). Distinguishing occasional abstention from routine indifference in models of vote choice. Political Science Research and Methods, 5(2), 277-294. doi:10.1017/psrm.2015.42

Greene, W.H. (1994). Accounting for excess zeros and sample selection in Poisson and negative binomial regression models. Working Paper EC-94-10, Stern School of Business, New York University.

Vuong, Q.H. (1989). Likelihood ratio tests for model selection and non-nested hypotheses. Econometrica, 57, 307-333. doi:10.2307/1912557

Wilson, P. (2015). The misuse of the Vuong test for non-nested models to test for zero-inflation. Economics Letters, 127, 51-53. doi:10.1016/j.econlet.2014.12.029

See also

lr_test(), compare_models()

Other model comparison: boot_lr_test(), classification(), compare_models(), fit_stats(), lr_test()

Examples

set.seed(2)
d <- rmnl(800, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(-0.3, 0.6, -0.5)),
          delta = c(0.5, 1.2), inflate = "a")
vuong(imnl(y ~ x1 + x2 | z1, data = d, inflate = "a"), mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d))
#> Vuong test:  m1 = imnl(y ~ x1 + x2 | z1, data = d, inflate = "a") [ Inflated multinomial logit (inflated alternative: a, logit split) ]
#>              m2 = mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d) [ Multinomial logit ]
#> positive statistics favor m1
#> 
#>  correction statistic p_m1_better p_m2_better p_two_sided
#>         raw     5.492           0           1           0
#>         AIC     5.294           0           1           0
#>         BIC     4.830           0           1           0
#> Note: The inflated multinomial logit and the multinomial logit are nested at the boundary phi = 1, where the normal reference does not hold for testing the uninflated model; boot_lr_test() calibrates the statistic.
